opening.headline: The reason why the scope of access expanded after sharing the assistant with the team is explained by the scope of sharing, level of access, and the risks of link sharing.
body: I shared the Human Resources Policy Assistant with several members of my team, but the link may spread and end up being opened by unintended people. Sharing speeds collaboration but also increases exposure.

In this lesson, we'll distinguish between sharing scopes - just me, team, and organization - and explore how access levels and link settings work in the project sharing screen. Next, we check the rules when group access and individual access overlap, the risks of link sharing, and provide a step-by-step explanation of the settings for sharing only with the human resources team.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain the scope of sharing across teams and organizational units
You can distinguish the exposure range by sharing method.

screens.title: When I shared it with the team, the reach expanded.
screens.lead: First, read the situation of the person who shared the HR policy assistant.

visual.alt: A concentric circle illustration that shows the overlap between the intention to share in a narrow scope and the actual broadened access target.
labels: Can be opened by unintentional people

paragraphs: A person in the human resources department shared a project to use the human resources policy assistant with several members of the team. I shared it as a link to make it easier to use, but as the link was sent through messenger, even unintended people could open it.

A project contains conversations, uploaded files, and instructions. The ChatGPT documentation explains that ChatGPT can pull content from anywhere in a shared project: conversations, uploaded files, and custom instructions. So, when you share a project, all of these become objects of sharing.
Instead of providing convenience, sharing broadens your exposure. You can weigh the pros and cons of sharing only when you know who you opened it to, in what way, and to what level.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: When sharing an assistant, which is easier to lose between 'who to show' and 'what to show'? We cover both in class.

screens.outro: First, let me recall how I identify what I share with.

screens.title: Do you verify the destination when creating a shared link?
screens.lead: If you first think about each question in your head and then select it, the instructor will organize your thoughts. You will not enter or submit an answer.

items.prompt: Lastly, can you tell me exactly who will view the material you shared?
items.answer: You remember it right after you share it, but it fades over time. The actual destination will change as group membership changes or the link is forwarded. Sharing is not something you set up once and is done; it is a state that needs to be checked again from time to time.

items.prompt: Do you know the difference between 'invitees only' and 'anyone with link'?
items.answer: I set a list of only the people I invite, and anyone with a link becomes the target. In the latter case, I have no control over the destination at the moment the link is delivered.

items.prompt: Have you ever thought that when you share, the files and instructions you uploaded will also be opened?
items.answer: When you share a project, you'll see your uploaded files and instructions as well as the conversation. Sensitive content contained in files can also be shared. You need to get into the habit of taking a quick look at what's in your project before sharing it.

screens.outro: Now let's see how the sharing scope is divided.

screens.title: Sharing scope: Just me, team, organization
screens.lead: Select each tab to see who can see each share.

tabs.label: Just me
tabs.body: This range is accessible only to the person who created it. When creating a project in Claude for the Team or Enterprise plan, if you select 'Invitees only', by default only you will have access, and conversations, project knowledge, and artifacts will not be visible to anyone who has not been explicitly invited. This is the narrowest scope, making it a good starting point for sharing settings.

tabs.label: team
tabs.body: It is a scope where specific individuals or groups are invited and only those who need it are used. ChatGPT allows Business, Enterprise, and Edu users to invite individuals or workspace groups, while Claude invites organization members by name or email, and the Enterprise plan also lets you add groups. When you invite, you set the level of access together.

tabs.label: organization
tabs.body: This range is accessible to all members of the organization. In Claude, if you select 'All organization members' when creating a project, it becomes a public project, and members can find it in the organization tab, open it, and start a conversation. Even if it is a public project, conversations within it are private until you share them directly. Knowledge and guidance from the project are shared.

tabs.label: Managed workspace
tabs.body: In ChatGPT's managed workspaces, project invitations can be limited to workspace members. The sharing method also varies depending on the workspace settings: individual invitation, group invitation, or workspace link. Remember that the sharing method you see on your screen is determined by your account and workspace settings.

tabs.label: Share GPT
tabs.body: GPTs can also be shared. When you select Share on the GPT editing screen, you can check the sharing options available in your account or workspace, and copy the GPT link from the more menu. GPT's name will remain visible in search results and shared links, so be careful not to reveal sensitive information in the name and description. In workspaces, GPT creation and sharing is controlled by permission settings.

screens.outro: Next, let's read the project sharing screen specifically.

screens.title: Reading the Project Sharing Settings screen
screens.lead: Select the arrows to read the ChatGPT project's share window from top to bottom.

visual.alt: Screen mockup of the project sharing window with invitations, access levels, and link settings divided into sections.

steps.title: Open the share window
steps.body: When you select Share in a project, the Share window opens. Depending on your plan and workspace settings, you may see individual invitations, group invitations, or project link sharing.

steps.title: Invite
steps.body: Free, Go, Plus, and Pro users can invite individuals with Only those invited, while Business, Enterprise, and Edu users can invite individuals or workspace groups. Enter your name, email, and group, select an access level, and select Invite. A confirmation email will be sent to the invitees and you.

steps.title: Chat and edit access levels
steps.body: Chat access allows you to view and interact with the project's conversations, files, and instructions, but cannot invite others. Edit access allows you to modify instructions, upload or delete files, and invite others. Existing members cannot be exported. Only the owner can set member permissions and delete projects.

steps.title: link settings
steps.body: The owner sets the link settings between Only those invited and Anyone with a link. If you leave it as Anyone with a link, any logged in ChatGPT user with the link can participate in the project. This setting can only be changed by the owner, and the owner can change the visibility settings at any time.

steps.title: Deletion from a shared project
steps.body: When you delete a file from a shared project, it disappears from all members. You can add it again. Therefore, it is best to give edit access only to those who need it.

screens.outro: Now let's look at the risks when group and individual access overlap, and when links spread.

screens.title: Dangers of group sharing and link sharing
screens.lead: Below is an example of a shared settings record created for illustrative purposes. When you select a highlighted passage, an explanation appears explaining how that setting affects exposure range.

data.text:
Project: Human Resources Regulations Assistant  
Link Settings: Anyone with a link  
Invited group: HR group, edit access  
Personal Adjustment: Reduce one member to chat access  
Project files: 12 personnel policy documents, 1 salary scale  
Project Guidelines: Always include article number with regulatory inquiries

marks.span: Link Settings: Anyone with a link
marks.note: This is the widest exposure factor. Any logged in ChatGPT user with the link can participate, and once the link spreads, it is difficult to control the audience. A narrow setting is to leave it to only the people you invite.

marks.span: Invited group: HR group, edit access
marks.note: When you invite a group to edit, all members of that group can edit instructions, add and delete files, and even invite others. Members who share the group will receive a notification, but people who later join the group will not receive a notification, but will be able to open it using the project address they received.

marks.span: Personal Adjustment: Reduce one member to chat access
marks.note: If groups and individuals have different access levels, whichever is higher applies. If the group is edit, edit is maintained even if the individual is lowered to chat. If you want to lower it, you should set the access level of the group itself to chat and raise only the necessary individuals to edit.

marks.span: Project files: 12 personnel policy documents, 1 salary scale
marks.note: When you share a project, files are also shared. Even though regulatory documents are fully visible to the HR team, you should consider removing sensitive files, such as salary rubrics, from the project before sharing them.

marks.span: Project Guidelines: Always include article number with regulatory inquiries
marks.note: Instructions are also shared and anyone with edit access can fix them. Guidelines change your assistant's behavior, so you need to narrow down who can fix them.

screens.outro: Now that we have identified the risk factors, we will explain the settings that are shared only with the HR team.

screens.title: Commentary: HR Policy Share Assistant only with HR
screens.lead: The instructor will explain the setup sequence to correct the first accident situation. Select the arrows and follow them step by step.

steps.title: 1. Start by keeping it private first
steps.body: Start with the narrowest scope. If you make a project private, only you can access it, and only necessary members will be invited to open it. If you open it as an organization-wide or link from the beginning and narrow it down later, there is no way to undo what has already been exposed in the meantime.

steps.title: 2. Invite the HR team via chat access
steps.body: Invite the HR team via chat access. Members can ask questions about the rules and get answers, but they cannot change the guidelines and files. For most users this should be sufficient.

steps.title: 3. Edit only for those in charge of modifying regulations
steps.body: Individual edits are given to only two or three people in charge of updating the regulations. Since you invited a group to chat, if you give edit to an individual, the higher one will be applied and only that person will be able to edit. Conversely, if you had invited a group to edit, lowering the individual level would have been useless.

steps.title: 4. Link sharing is only for those invited
steps.body: Leave the link setting to Only those invited. Then, even if the link is delivered, uninvited people will not be able to participate. It's a choice that gives up some convenience and gains control.

steps.title: 5. Also check administrator settings
steps.body: We also look at organization-level settings. In Claude, possible sharing depends on whether the administrator has Share projects or Public projects turned on, and in managed workspaces, invitations may be limited to members. Verify that the settings you've made and your organization's policies work together.

screens.outro: Once you have completed the settings, you must check the exposure targets even after sharing.

screens.title: Commentary: Check exposure targets after sharing
screens.lead: When you select each inspection item, the instructor's commentary will unfold. Here are four things to check after you've finished setting up sharing.

items.prompt: Have you read the individual, group, and link access in the sharing window one more time?
items.answer: After completing the settings, open the sharing window again and visually check the accessor list and link settings. The most obvious check is to compare the intended target with the actual list.

items.prompt: Did you know that when group membership changes, accessors also change?
items.answer: When shared as a group, new members of the group can also open the project, and those who have left have fewer access paths. As the personnel of the human resources team changes, the project's accessors also change. This is why you should check your group composition regularly.

items.prompt: Have you identified whether conversations are private or project knowledge is shared?
items.answer: In Claude, even if your project is public, conversations within it are private until you share them directly, but project knowledge and guidance are shared. You must be aware of the distinction between dialogue being hidden and data being visible so that you can decide what to include in the project.

items.prompt: Has it been opened only to the extent necessary for convenience?
items.answer: It is enough to provide convenience only to those who need it. Unnecessarily wide access can be narrowed at any time, but information that has already been exposed cannot be removed. If in doubt, keep it narrow, and open it when a request arises.

screens.outro: Now let's get to the point.

screens.title: Sharing is an exchange of convenience and exposure
screens.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class.

paragraphs: Sharing speeds up collaboration but broadens your reach. Start with the narrowest scope—Just Me, Team, or Organization—and open only as much as you need.

Access levels are divided into chat and edit. Remember that when group and individual access overlap, whichever is higher applies, and sharing links makes it harder to control your audience. And that includes not only conversations, but also files and instructions.

callout.label: something to remember
callout.text: Open from the narrowest scope, allow editing only to those who absolutely need it, and limit link sharing to invited people.

checks.q: In a project where the HR team was invited as editors, only one member had access to chat. What is the member’s actual level of access?
options: Changes to the value set by the administrator
checks.explain: If group access and individual access are different, the higher of the two applies, so the group's edits are maintained.

wrong.0: Personal settings will not overwrite group settings, whichever is higher will be applied.
wrong.2: Reducing individual access does not eliminate group access.
wrong.3: This rule is determined by comparing group and individual access, regardless of whether the administrator changes the value.

checks.intro: Check for yourself what you just learned. Results are not recorded.

checks.q: Put your HR policies assistant in the right order to share only with your HR team.
items: Keep it private and invite only necessary members
Invite the HR team via chat access
Edits are given to only two or three people in charge of modifying the rules.
Set link sharing to Only those invited
checks.explain: Start with the narrowest scope, open only as much as you need, and limit link sharing to only those you invite.
checks.intro: Put them in order, remembering the order you learned them. Results are not recorded.

glossary.def: This is the range of audiences who can view and use the data, such as just me, the team, or the organization.
A setting that opens a project containing conversations, files, and instructions to be shared with others.
Chat is the right to view and talk about the project, and edit is the right to edit instructions and files and invite others.
The point is that the person with the link soon becomes the target, making it difficult to control the scope of exposure.

misconceptions.myth: Even if you share a project, all your conversations are private.
misconceptions.fact: In Claude, even if your project is public, conversations within it are private until you share them directly. However, project knowledge and guidance are shared. ChatGPT allows ChatGPT to utilize conversations, files, and instructions from shared projects.

misconceptions.myth: Links are convenient, so you can always leave it as Anyone with a link.
misconceptions.fact: Once a link is forwarded, you have no control over its destination. It's safer to start with only invited people and expand only when absolutely necessary.

misconceptions.myth: If you invite a group to edit and then lower an individual to chat, that person becomes chat.
misconceptions.fact: If groups and individuals have different access levels, the higher one applies. Even if you invite a group to edit and then lower the individual to chat, edit will remain.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: Sharing is an exchange of convenience and exposure.
Open the narrowest settings: Just Me, Team, or Organization.
Differentiate between chat and edit access levels.
Link sharing is limited to those you invite.
